title: German Foreign Office → German Legation Stockholm, numeric-code telegrams obtained by the US Legation Stockholm (indicator groups 017/010/693)
correspondents: Auswärtiges Amt, Berlin (signed Stumm, Bussche, 'auswaertig') → Deutsche Gesandtschaft Stockholm
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Decimal File 763.72/11631, 11654, 11668 and enclosures of Stockholm despatches 1421 (4 Oct 1918), 1426 (8 Oct 1918), 1475 (6 Nov 1918); microfilm M367 rolls 108, 114, 122, 141
folio_note: Telegraph-form copies with full German headers (w-numbers, word counts, dates): M367 roll 114 frames 0415-0418 (desp. 1421: nos. 1-3), roll 141 frames 1255-1265 (desp. 1426: ten telegrams, incl. 017 733 405, 017 435 437 693, 017 149 405, 017 963 405, 017 556 405, 010 018 406), roll 122 frames 0154-0155 (desp. 1475: 017 119 943). why: German Foreign Office instructions to its Stockholm legation in the last months of the war (July 1918), obtained by US diplomats; content unknown.

title: Bernstorff (German Embassy Washington) → German Foreign Office, cipher telegram on armed merchantmen sent through the State Department cable
correspondents: Count Johann Heinrich von Bernstorff → Auswärtiges Amt, Berlin (via Secretary Lansing and Amembassy Berlin)
folio_note: Roll 166 frames 0785-0786: the cipher text (about 150 groups of 3-5 digits, e.g. 958 677 728 229 0705 1166 0352 7031 ...; frame 0786 is a reversed/offset image). Frames 0769-0775 hold the German memorandum on armed merchant vessels (in clear) and 0778-0784 its English translation; 0787-0789 Lansing's note of 10 Jan 1917 and the 'TELEGRAM SENT ... Please deliver following cipher to Foreign Office, from German Ambassador here' of 11 Jan 1917; 0790-0795 Lansing-Wilson letters of 22 and 31 Jan 1917.
status: Filed without a decode. The memorandum Bernstorff delivered to Lansing the day before is filed in clear beside it and is very probably the plaintext or its basis (a crib). Same channel as the Zimmermann telegram five days later; German traffic on it was in code 13040 or 0075. Distinct from catalogue entry 'German Foreign Office → Bernstorff, 5 Dec 1916' (FRUS sweep). Not on DECODE.
why: A German Embassy code telegram of the last weeks before unrestricted U-boat warfare, with a near-certain crib; a test of the 13040/0075 codes on known text.
score_note: Scored from the NARA OCR of the scans during the Oct 2026 NARA bulk-scan triage (research/nara_triage_b/); image not viewed
verify: View roll 166 frames 0785-0786 and transcribe; check Room 40 decrypts (TNA HW 7, ADM 223/ADM 137) for 11 Jan 1917; align with the German memorandum text (frames 0769-0775).

title: German Minister at Lima (Perl) ↔ German legations Santiago, Buenos Aires, Montevideo, Mexico: copies of cipher telegrams obtained by the US Legation Lima
correspondents: German Legation Lima (Minister Perl; later Weyers) ↔ German legations in Santiago, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Mexico
shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Central Decimal File 1910-29, 862.20223 (German military activities in Peru), sub-nos. 4-99
folio_note: Known only from the purport list (M973 roll 207 frames 1008-1014): about 70 cables from Callao-Lima each transmitting 1-7 'telegrams in German cipher' (June 1917 - Jan 1918), Lima despatch 342 of 6 June 1917 'copies of cipher code messages exchanged between German diplomatic officers', and the Department's relays 'FOR BELL FROM HARRISON' to London. The 862.20223 file itself is not among the scanned frames.
status: Partially read at the time: London (Bell / Gunther, i.e. Room 40 via the US Embassy) cabled back the 'substance' of most batches; Lima 85 (9 Oct 1917) reports some messages could not be deciphered. Verbatim decodes not listed. Not on DECODE; not in the repo.
why: German diplomatic traffic along the west coast of South America in 1917, with a contemporary partial reading to check against.
